title: IndiGo Dubai-Mumbai Flight Makes Emergency Landing in Rajkot After Cargo Smoke Alert
excerpt: All 194 people on board IndiGo flight 6E 1452 were safely evacuated at Rajkot International Airport after smoke was detected in the cargo hold, prompting a full emergency declaration.
body:
• IndiGo flight 6E 1452 from Dubai to Mumbai made an emergency landing at Rajkot International Airport after smoke was detected in the cargo hold.
  • All 194 people on board disembarked safely with no injuries reported.
  • Rajkot airport declared a full emergency at 2:45 PM; the aircraft landed at 3:27 PM.
  • IndiGo is arranging an alternate aircraft while the plane undergoes inspection.

An IndiGo flight carrying 194 people from Dubai to Mumbai was forced to make an emergency landing at Rajkot International Airport in Gujarat on Monday after the crew detected smoke in the aircraft's cargo hold.

IndiGo flight 6E 1452, also designated IGO1452, departed Dubai on a routine journey to Mumbai when a smoke alert was triggered in the cargo compartment mid-flight. The pilots immediately decided to divert the aircraft to the nearest available airport.

Full Emergency Declared at Rajkot

Rajkot International Airport Director Digant Borah said a full emergency was declared at 2:45 PM after the airport received information about the smoke alert. The aircraft made a safe emergency landing at 3:27 PM, roughly 42 minutes after the emergency was declared.

https://x.com/TimesNow/status/2081732223968108790

"An IndiGo flight operating from Dubai to Mumbai made an emergency landing at Rajkot airport after smoke was detected in the cargo hold area. The aircraft landed safely, and all passengers are safe."

— Digant Borah, Rajkot Airport Director

All 194 people on board — passengers and crew — disembarked the aircraft safely. No injuries were reported.

Emergency Response Mobilized

Rajkot authorities launched a swift emergency response as soon as the airport received word of the incoming distressed aircraft. The Rajkot Municipal Corporation dispatched two fire engines and two ambulances to the airport, according to Dainik Bhaskar. Firefighters and medical teams remained on standby throughout the operation.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=dkMfnIbb_Kk

Personnel from the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), airport police, and other emergency agencies reached the airport to assist with the evacuation and secure the area. As a precautionary measure, bomb disposal and sniffer dog squads were also deployed at the airport.

IndiGo Arranging Alternate Aircraft

IndiGo confirmed the emergency landing in a statement, saying the aircraft is undergoing inspection before it can be cleared to resume operations.

"An alternate aircraft is being arranged to complete the journey and in the meantime, we are assisting our customers and making all necessary arrangements to ease the waiting time."

— IndiGo statement

The airline said it "sincerely regrets the inconvenience caused" and emphasized that passenger and crew safety remains its top priority.

A Key Route for the Indian Diaspora

The Dubai-Mumbai corridor is one of the busiest international air routes connecting India to the Gulf region. Millions of Indian expatriates live and work in the United Arab Emirates, and the route sees heavy traffic from workers, families, and business travelers year-round. IndiGo, India's largest airline by market share, operates multiple daily flights between the two cities.

The airline flies to over 80 domestic and more than 30 international destinations, operating Airbus A320 and A321 series aircraft along with ATR 72-600 turboprops, according to NDTV.

What's Next

The cause of the cargo smoke alert has not yet been confirmed. Aviation authorities are expected to investigate whether the alarm was triggered by an actual fire, a sensor malfunction, or another issue. India's Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) typically reviews such incidents as part of standard safety protocols.

Passengers stranded at Rajkot will be accommodated on the alternate aircraft IndiGo is arranging. The airline has not provided a timeline for when the replacement flight will depart.
